title: Extract weight deserializers into shared service and align lexicon (tokenizer) contract
creator: Diego Ramirez
description:
Background: Over time the model ingest pipeline accrued multiple ad-hoc weight deserializers and tokenizer handoffs. Different model formats (legacy ckpt, v2 manifest, shard-indexed) each implemented deserialization logic inline with asset loaders. This has caused duplicated parsing logic, inconsistent error semantics, and brittle tokenizer alignment when partial weight activation occurs (stale vocab boundaries, off-by-one token offsets during streaming activation).

Goal: Create a single shared Weight Deserialization Service (WDS) responsible for canonicalizing weight blobs into a uniform in-memory representation and exposing a small, stable contract for tokenizer/lexicon alignment. The WDS will:
- Support current formats (legacy-ckpt, v2-shard-index, streaming-manifest) via adapters loaded at startup.
- Emit deterministic shard boundary metadata and token-alignment maps so the tokenizer handshake can validate prefix/offset consistency.
- Provide a bump-safe versioning header so serving runtime can fall back to compatible loader adapters.

Non-goals: Converting model artifacts on disk or migrating existing customer checkpoints. This ticket focuses on runtime deserialization and contract stabilization, not migration tools.

Design notes:
- New module: internal/wds (language: Rust for safety and current runtime parity). Exposes a gRPC-like local socket API to runtime workers to request deserialization for a given asset URI and shard range. Returns: canonical weight descriptor (identifier, dtype, shape metadata, shard-keys), activation plan (ordered segments), and token-alignment manifest (vocab slices + absolute token indices).
- Adapter pattern: each format implements Adapter::probe(uri) -> confidence, Adapter::deserialize(stream) -> canonical. Adapters run in separate worker-thread pools, with a per-adapter time budget to protect serving latency.
- Tokenizer contract: Lexicon adapter must accept token-alignment manifest and reply with a validation status and an optional remap table when vocab slices overlap or use legacy encodings. Remap tables are opaque to runtime but must be stable across restarts.
- Backward compatibility: Introduce a compatibility shim in runtime that maps old inline loader responses to the new canonical descriptor. This shim lives in internal/model-ingest/compat and is removed once consumers have migrated (follow-up ticket).

Rollout plan:
1) Implement WDS and Adapter interface behind feature flag wds-enabled=false. Unit tests and integration tests. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rw/runtime/pull/1227)
2) Wire runtime to call WDS for model loads where feature flag enabled. Keep old code path as fallback. Run canary on staging for nightly models. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rw/runtime/pull/1234)
3) Enable wds-enabled=true for dedicated integration tests and watch for regressions for two weeks. If stable, flip for more environments and create deprecation window for inline deserializers.

Testing and validation:
- Unit adapters for each format with golden artifacts (small fixtures).
- End-to-end tests that load multi-sharded Llama-like and GPT-like fixtures, validate token-alignment manifest against tokenizer output.
- Chaos test: force partial shard activation and verify that tokenizer remap table prevents off-by-one token errors.
- Performance test: measure median first-chunk model load latency with WDS on vs. old path; cap acceptable regression at +10% for cold load but target improvement for memory usage due to deduped parsing.

Metrics to watch:
- model_load_cold_ms (p50/p95),
- tokenizer_alignment_errors (count),
- wds_adapter_failures (count, by adapter),
- memory_peak_during_deserialize_mb.

Risks:
- Small increase in cold-start latency due to IPC to WDS; mitigated by co-locating WDS and using unix domain sockets and shared mmap for large shard reads.
- Adapter bugs could surface with obscure checkpoint formats; mitigate with canary scope and strong fixture coverage.

Acceptance criteria:
- WDS implemented and exercised by unit/integration tests.
- Tokenizer alignment manifest validated in E2E tests for at least 3 representative model families.
- No increase >10% in p95 cold load latency in canary cluster; tokenization errors reduced to zero on test fixtures.
- Documentation updated (Confluence link) with adapter guide and contract spec.

Docs / links:
- Design spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ML/Weight+Deserialization+Service+Design
- PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw/runtime/pull/1227
- Canary run dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/model-loads/wds-canary

Next steps / follow-ups:
- ENG-213580: migrate one serving fleet to wds-enabled=true (canary manual flip).
- ENG-213581: remove legacy inline loader code and delete compat shim after deprecation window.

Notes on implementation trade-offs:
- Language choice (Rust) chosen for memory safety and better interop with existing runtime slices. Alternative was to keep in Go for faster dev; rejected due to previous memory-safety incidents during streaming activation.
- IPC vs in-process: IPC chosen to maintain a single stabilizing process and simplify adapter crash isolation. In-process would be faster but increases blast radius.
